title: Lift normalized polynomial coordinates and compute the image prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$, $E=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $\mathfrak q'\subset E$ a prime with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q'\cap R$. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $Q=\ker(E\otimes_R k\to\kappa(\mathfrak q'))$, viewed as a prime of $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ via coefficient scalar extension [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(Q)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then $r$ is a nonnegative integer with $r\le n$, and there exist $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and an $R_f$-algebra homomorphism $\psi:C=R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to D=R_f[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] such that $D$ is of finite type over $C$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], its scalar extension $\bar\psi:k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ is finite (the target is finitely generated as a module over the source [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]), and $\bar\psi^{-1}(Q)=I=(x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n)$. For $\mathfrak q_D=\mathfrak q'D$ and $P=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_D)$ one has $P=(\mathfrak pR_f,x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n)$, and the prime of $C\otimes_{R_f}k=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ corresponding to $P$ is exactly $I$.

source.place: Tag 0520 (lemma-refined-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra), proof, from the image prime through lifting the coordinates; Tag 051P (lemma-refined-Noether-normalization). The prescribed inverse-image ideal is computed coefficientwise.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields] to $R\to E$ at $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q'$, and identify the fibre with $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]. Thus $Q$ is prime and the coefficient map $j:E\to k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ has $j^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak q'$. Put $B=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/Q$. By the fraction description of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\kappa(Q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$: a fraction in the local ring modulo its maximal ideal is exactly $\bar a/\bar b$, with $b\notin Q$. Let $s$ be the set of the $n$ variable images in this field. Its generated $k$-subalgebra is $B$. Every element $a/b$ of the field satisfies the nonzero polynomial $bT-a\in B[T]$, since $b\ne0$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-algebraic-adjoin-transcendence-bound] therefore hold, so $r\le |s|\le n$. A cardinal bounded by the finite integer $n$ is a nonnegative integer.

source.place: Tag 0520, lemma-refined-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, image fibre prime; Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization, parameter r. The explicit bound uses the existing Mathlib algebraic-adjoin lemma.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-refined-noether-normalization-prime] with the field $k$, the integer $n$ and the prime $Q$. It gives a finite $k$-algebra map $\varphi:k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ with $\varphi^{-1}(Q)=I=(x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n)$. Write $\bar h_i=\varphi(x_i)$. Finiteness here is exactly finite generation of the target module, as required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 051P, lemma-refined-Noether-normalization; its application in Tag 0520.

proof.text: There are finitely many nonzero coefficients in the $n$ polynomials $\bar h_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], each coefficient of $k=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is represented by some $a/b$ with $a\in R$ and $b\notin\mathfrak p$. Choose such representatives, and let $f$ be the product of all these denominators (the empty product is $1$). Primality gives $f\notin\mathfrak p$. For each chosen denominator $b$, write $f=bc$ using the other factors; its chosen coefficient lifts to $ac/f\in R_f$. Keeping the same monomials defines $h_i\in D=R_f[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ reducing to $\bar h_i$. These fractions are legitimate by [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 0520, sentence choosing f and the lifts h_i; expanded coefficient by coefficient.

proof.text: The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives the $R_f$-algebra map $\psi:C=R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to D$ sending $x_i$ to $h_i$. The $n$ elements $t_i$ generate $D$ as a $C$-algebra: a polynomial in the $t_i$ already has coefficients in $R_f$, which is in the image of $C$. This proves finite type by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Via [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], tensoring with $k$ sends $x_i$ to $\bar h_i$, so uniqueness in the same universal property gives $\bar\psi=\varphi$. It is finite and has inverse-image ideal $I$ by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0520, lifted polynomial map and its scalar extension.

proof.text: Let $\delta:D\to k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and $\rho:C\to k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be coefficient maps. The ring $D$ is the localization $E_f$: multiplying the finitely many coefficient denominators in a polynomial writes every element as $G/f^m$, and the fraction equality relation is coefficientwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $\mathfrak q_D=\mathfrak q'D$ is prime, since $f\notin\mathfrak q'$. For $G/f^m\in D$, $\delta(G/f^m)\in Q$ iff $j(G)\in Q$, because $j(f)$ is a nonzero scalar; by Step 1 this is equivalent to $G\in\mathfrak q'$, hence to $G/f^m\in\mathfrak q_D$. Thus $\delta^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak q_D$. On coefficients and variables, $\delta\psi=\varphi\rho$, so $P=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_D)=\rho^{-1}(I)$.

source.place: Tag 0520, image prime after lifting; Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization, in the cited localization lemma.

proof.text: The coefficient map $R_f\to k$ has kernel $\mathfrak pR_f$: for $a/f^m$, its image is zero iff some $b\notin\mathfrak p$ has $ba\in\mathfrak p$, which by primality is equivalent to $a\in\mathfrak p$. A polynomial $H\in C$ belongs to $\rho^{-1}(I)$ iff setting $x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n$ to zero in $\rho(H)$ gives zero. By coefficient uniqueness, this says precisely that every coefficient of $H$ on a monomial involving only $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ lies in $\mathfrak pR_f$. Those terms belong to $\mathfrak pC$; each remaining monomial is divisible by one of $x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n$. Conversely each generator of $(\mathfrak pR_f,x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n)$ maps into $I$. Therefore $P=(\mathfrak pR_f,x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n)$. Its contraction to $R_f$ is $\mathfrak pR_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], this prime has residue field canonically $k$. By the bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields] and the polynomial scalar-extension isomorphism, $I$ is exactly the prime corresponding to $P$, since its inverse image is $P$.

source.place: Tag 0520, prescribed inverse-image ideal, computed coefficientwise; fibre prime correspondence in the cited node.

lean.statement: theorem normalizedPolynomialPrimeLift (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (q : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) (hp : p.asIdeal = q.asIdeal.under R) : ∃ r : ℕ, Algebra.trdeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField (polynomialFibrePrime R n p q hp).asIdeal.ResidueField = (r : Cardinal) ∧ r ≤ n ∧ ∃ (f : R) (hf : f ∉ p.asIdeal) (ψ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (Localization.Away f) →ₐ[Localization.Away f] MvPolynomial (Fin n) (Localization.Away f)), ψ.toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ (polynomialMapResidueReduction R n p f hf ψ).toRingHom.Finite ∧ Ideal.comap (polynomialMapResidueReduction R n p f hf ψ).toRingHom (polynomialFibrePrime R n p q hp).asIdeal = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ if r ≤ i.val then MvPolynomial.X i else 0)) ∧ Ideal.comap ψ.toRingHom (q.asIdeal.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f)))) = p.asIdeal.map (MvPolynomial.C.comp (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))) ⊔ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ if r ≤ i.val then MvPolynomial.X i else 0)) ∧ Ideal.comap (MvPolynomial.map (polynomialAwayResidueMap R p f hf)) (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ if r ≤ i.val then MvPolynomial.X i else 0))) = Ideal.comap ψ.toRingHom (q.asIdeal.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))))
lean.note: The three auxiliary definitions give the canonical fibre prime, localization coefficient map, and reduced polynomial algebra map used in the theorem. The final contraction equality specifies the fibre prime corresponding to P.
